ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rhombus $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. $H$ is the midpoint of side $AD$. If the perimeter of rhombus $ABCD$ is $40$, what is the length of $OH$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since the perimeter of the rhombus ABCD is 40,\\
therefore $CD=10$,\\
and since H is the midpoint of side AD and point O is the midpoint of AC,\\
therefore $OH$ is the median of $\triangle ACD$,\\
therefore $OH=\frac{1}{2}CD=\frac{1}{2} \times 10=\boxed{5}$.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/vector setup centered at O. From the image, take O as the intersection of the diagonals, with A and C opposite each other and B and D opposite each other, and H on AD. From the text, ABCD is a rhombus and H is the midpoint of AD. Let O be the origin and write the position vectors of A and D as a and d. Because the diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, C has vector -a and B has vector -d. Since H is the midpoint of AD, the vector OH is (a + d)/2. Also the side AD has vector d - a, while side CD has vector d - (-a) = a + d. In a rhombus all sides are equal, so CD = AD = 40/4 = 10; equivalently |a + d| = 10. Hence OH = |(a + d)/2| = 5.
